column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says You bring me to judgment; BSB says him.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew begins if, where BSB says since.
The Hebrew says until rather than so that.
The Hebrew has its shoot in the singular; BSB uses shoots.
The Hebrew has root in the singular; BSB says roots.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew presents the waters disappearing as a completed action.
The Hebrew shifts from a man in the singular to they and their sleep; BSB keeps he.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew begins if; BSB says when. Again is not explicitly stated.
The Hebrew explicitly says I will answer You.
The Hebrew says now; BSB says then.
The Hebrew says the transgression is sealed, without an explicit would be.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew presents Your destroying hope with a completed verb; BSB uses a present description.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew coordinates his sons’ honor or humiliation with his ignorance; BSB uses conditional clauses.
The Hebrew makes his flesh the subject of pain and his soul the subject of mourning; BSB makes him the experiencer of both.
